original.title: The Modern Practice of Adult Education: From Pedagogy to Andragogy
original.note: Library record's first publication year is 1970; 1980 is the edition or translation cited here.

core_idea: Adults learn differently from children. Knowles's assumptions: adults are self-directed, bring experience, learn when it meets a real need, prefer problem-centred learning and are motivated from within.
key_concepts_note: Use the concepts already stored for this theory in the library (theories.concepts).
when_to_use: How do adult learners experience a training or degree programme?
How should professional development be designed for adults?
Typical data: interviews, surveys, programme evaluation.
common_mistakes: Treating the assumptions as proven facts about all adults rather than as a set of design assumptions.
Opposing andragogy to pedagogy as if children never learn this way.
Ignoring culture: the self-directed learner is a Western ideal.
